entries.clue: Skip lectures going ahead to discuss job (4,4)

indicatorNotes.going ahead: the lectures move in front of the skip

annotation.surface: A student skips lectures and heads off to chat about work.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue gives the skip first, but the lectures go ahead of it, so TALKS leads.
annotation.definitionFit: To talk shop is to discuss your work, often when others would rather you didn't.

entries.clue: Snag bottom of buggy with stone (4)

indicatorNotes.bottom of: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a rub = a snag, as in 'there's the rub'

annotation.surface: A pushchair catches on a stone in the path.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snag' looks like a verb acting on the buggy; it is the noun, a difficulty.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ruby is one kind of gemstone, and jewellers still call gems stones.

entries.clue: Aim to sort out job etc (6)

indicatorNotes.to sort out: sorting out puts the letters in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone sets out to tidy up a job and its loose ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'etc' is a giveaway that the letters are the fodder: few clues end on it otherwise.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of purpose: the object of an exercise is what you are aiming at.

entries.clue: Distinctive cup laced with drug caught deceiver (8)

indicatorNotes.laced: letters laced together are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: CUP plus E (ecstasy, the drug) twisted together

annotation.surface: A cheat is caught spiking a drink with drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Laced' pretends to mean a spiked drink, which fits the surface perfectly; here it works the letters of CUP and E into PECU. 'Caught' only joins the halves.
annotation.definitionFit: Something peculiar is distinctive, belonging to one thing alone.

entries.clue: Dawned fair at sea and throughout the land (3,3,4)

indicatorNotes.at sea: at sea = confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A fine morning broke over the ocean and across the country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the weather picture so well that it hides its job of mixing the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: covering ground both distant and broad, it means over the whole country or everywhere.

entries.clue: Break promise about turning over online information (6)

indicatorNotes.turning over: turned over, the letters run the other way

blocks.note: re = about, as in a memo heading

annotation.surface: Someone backs out of a deal after reading the small print online.
annotation.walkthrough: E plus GEN is turned over as one piece to give NEGE. GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: going back on your word, originally a card-game term for failing to follow suit.

entries.clue: Blue lava sculpture’s worth a lot of money (8)

indicatorNotes.sculpture’s: a sculpture is material reshaped, so the letters are remodelled

annotation.surface: An artwork carved from blue volcanic rock fetches a high price.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'sculpture's' reads as 'is' in the surface and also as 'sculpture of'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the adjective: of high monetary worth, like a prized sculpture.

entries.clue: Forgive former copper’s heartless side (6)

indicatorNotes.heartless: the heart, the middle letters, comes out

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A retired policeman is pardoned despite his callous streak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' pushes toward a policeman; it is the metal. Copper is British slang for police officer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to pardon an offence or let someone off it.

entries.clue: Some millionaires are backing rubber (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: the tail of millionaires and all of are, to be read right to left

annotation.surface: A few rich people are investing in a rubber company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as financial support in the surface. In Britain a rubber is an eraser.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British schoolchildren call the thing that rubs out pencil marks a rubber.

entries.clue: Oak-fermented chardonnay’s finish is not bad (4)

indicatorNotes.fermented: fermenting changes the stuff, so the letters are altered
indicatorNotes.finish: the finish of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A wine critic gives an oaked chardonnay a lukewarm verdict.
annotation.walkthrough: The wine-tasting words 'oak', 'fermented' and 'finish' all do mechanical jobs here.
annotation.definitionFit: Okay is a grudging 'not bad'.

entries.clue: Stimulated by beer in extremity (10)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: Courage is a British brewery and its beer

annotation.surface: Someone is spurred on by a drink in desperate straits.
annotation.walkthrough: Courage is an English beer brand; the surface's hint of Dutch courage, drink-fuelled bravery, helps.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the past participle: given heart, spurred on, stirred to act.

entries.clue: What’s wrong’s right to prevent (6)

indicatorNotes.wrong: put wrong, the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A moralist says setting things right is about stopping wrongdoing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What's wrong' reads as a question about a problem; it is WHAT with an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to block or frustrate someone's plan.

entries.clue: Cheers up everyone getting booking that’s very difficult (1,4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is a noun phrase: a task that's very difficult

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

annotation.surface: Everyone's spirits lift when a hard-to-get reservation comes through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers up' looks like 'brightens'; it is TA written upwards. Ta is British for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an order or demand so tall it is hard to reach, a task that is very difficult.

entries.clue: Superficial view without understanding’s beginning to provoke (4-4)

indicatorNotes.without: without = outside, so the view goes round
indicatorNotes.beginning: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A shallow opinion with no insight is bound to stir up trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old sense 'outside', not 'lacking', and 'understanding' is the adjective (sympathetic), not the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Skin-deep means superficial, going no further than the surface.

entries.clue: Zoopla queries content of commemorative tablet (6)

indicatorNotes.content of: the answer is the content, sitting inside

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words, after zoo and before ries

annotation.surface: A property website asks about a blue plaque on a house.
annotation.walkthrough: Zoopla is a British property-listing website; the surface fits a house with a memorial tablet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plaque is a tablet fixed to a wall to commemorate someone.

entries.clue: A French writer has poem which contains absolutely everything (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

blocks.note: the writer of the clue, me = I

annotation.surface: A French author writes an all-encompassing poem.
annotation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, who calls himself I. The definition is a description rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition describes rather than names: the cosmos is the sum of all that exists.

entries.clue: Pronounced cups of tea required for injury (6)

indicatorNotes.Pronounced: said out loud rather than spelt

annotation.surface: A cup of tea is prescribed for someone who's been hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' pretends to mean 'marked', strong tea. A brew is British informal for a cup of tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a discoloured patch from a knock is one kind of injury.

entries.clue: Massive house’s south side has fancy sunroom (8)

indicatorNotes.south side: in a down clue the south side of a word is its bottom, last letter
indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy = elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An estate agent boasts of a huge house with a smart conservatory on its south face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South side' is estate-agent language for a sunny aspect; in a down clue it points at the bottom letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the adjective: huge in size, as the surface's grand house is.

entries.clue: Child with regularly kooky education stifled (6)

annotation.surface: A child with oddball schooling finds themselves held back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply adds the pieces in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the past participle: suffocated or strangled, both meaning cut off from air.

entries.clue: Nearly Spring with reduced darkness (4-4)

indicatorNotes.reduced: reduced = shortened, losing its last letter

blocks.note: a well is a spring of water

annotation.surface: Spring is almost here and the evenings are getting lighter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, and its capital letter helps the disguise; it is a source of water.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned idiom: 'nigh' already means near, and 'well' intensifies it to almost.

entries.clue: Fairly likely to be gutted after fixture’s cut short (6)

indicatorNotes.to be gutted: gutting removes the insides, leaving the outer letters
indicatorNotes.after: this piece comes after the other
indicatorNotes.cut short: cut short loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A football fan predicts they'll probably be devastated after the match is abandoned early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' is a sports event, British usage for a scheduled match.
annotation.definitionFit: Evenly means fairly, with equal shares.

entries.clue: Minor earthquake set back capital city, centre of Khartoum (6)

indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: khaRToum, the middle two of eight letters

annotation.surface: A small quake jolts a capital and shakes central Khartoum.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together, so the Khartoum letters end up at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a small shaking of the ground, the mildest kind of quake.

entries.clue: Central character in costume by Zara enlivened new Disney film (6)

indicatorNotes.Central character in: the central character of a word is its middle letter
indicatorNotes.enlivened: livened up, the letters are shaken about

annotation.surface: A fashion chain makes the lead's outfit for a new Disney release.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Central character' pretends to be the film's hero, which Tarzan is; it takes one letter. Zara is a clothing chain.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the ape-man story was made into an animated feature by Disney in 1999.

entries.clue: Snatch drink by river before reflecting on sad film (4-6)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: a reflection shows the letters backwards

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a drink by the riverside, musing on a melancholy film.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink by the river goes before the snatch, so TEAR leads; 'on' is RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A tearjerker is a sentimental film meant to make you cry.

entries.clue: Search for male riding horse (4)

indicatorNotes.riding: the male sits in the saddle, inside the horse

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy type of horse

annotation.surface: A search is on for the man who rode off on a horse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Search for' reads as one phrase, but 'for' only links.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: going through an area as thoroughly as teeth go through hair.

entries.clue: Loves entering cold Lake Placid (4)

indicatorNotes.entering: something entering a room goes inside it, so the loves go inside cold plus lake

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap
love = zero in tennis scores, O

annotation.surface: Lovers take a chilly dip in Lake Placid.
annotation.walkthrough: Lake Placid is a real place in New York, which hides the definition in the name.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the adjective: calm and unruffled, not hot-headed.

entries.clue: Doctor cures large penetrating sores (6)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: doctor = tamper with, so the letters change
indicatorNotes.penetrating: one piece goes into the other

annotation.surface: A physician heals big deep wounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' pretends to be a person in a medical scene; it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, in the plural: open, inflamed patches on skin or in the stomach lining.

entries.clue: Phone European Union to progress returning discussion (8)

indicatorNotes.returning: returning = coming back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A call to Brussels urges talks to move forward again.
annotation.walkthrough: EU and GO together are turned back to give OGUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the noun: talks between two sides, as in diplomatic dialogue.
